title: Which drug candidates deserve the next round?
prompt:
Create a large 16:9 landscape infographic for a general professional audience (managers, engineers new to the topic, students), light near-white background, warm and clear like a well-designed museum explainer or a quality newspaper graphic. Plain everyday language is the main text; technical names appear only as small grey secondary labels.

TITLE (large): "Which drug candidates deserve the next round?"
SUBTITLE: "TOKN screened six early compounds for safety red flags before anyone spent more time or money on them."

BAND 1 — heading "Why this matters": one wide card with a simple flat illustration of a molecule model beside a lab flask, and this text: "Most drug candidates fail late, after years of expensive work. Catching heart-safety, DNA-damage and drug-interaction risks early saves both."

BAND 2 — heading "Who did the work": a left-to-right flow of eight round role badges joined by arrows. Each badge shows a line icon, the bold role name, the short description in quotes, and the model name tiny and grey below:
1 Scout — "lists the tools available" (claude-haiku-5.5) [icon: binoculars]
2 Planner — "writes what 'done' looks like" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: document]
3 Analyst — "runs the official checks" (Kimi-K3.1-Pro) [icon: bar chart]
4 Skeptic — "re-checks and finds 9 weak spots" (FW-GLM-5.3) [icon: shield]
5 Judge — "decides: revise or ship?" (Microsoft-Decision-1) [icon: balance scale]
6 Editor — "fixes every weak spot" (gpt-6.1-sol) [icon: pencil]
7 Coach — "writes a lesson for next time" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: lightbulb]
8 Examiner — "scores it with plain code, no AI" (verify.py) [icon: checklist]
Caption under the flow: "Like a newsroom: a writer, a fact-checker, an editor — and an exam nobody can sweet-talk."

BAND 3 — heading "Four questions every compound must answer": four cards in a row, each with an icon, the question in large plain words, and a tiny grey tool label:
(DNA helix icon) "Could it damage DNA?" — tiny grey label: Ames · check_advancement_gate
(heart with a pulse line icon) "Could it disturb the heart's rhythm?" — tiny grey label: hERG · check_advancement_gate
(two capsules icon) "Could it clash with other medicines?" — tiny grey label: CYP3A4 · check_advancement_gate
(ruler beside a molecule icon) "Is the molecule a sensible size and shape?" — tiny grey label: compute_2d_properties · pains_filter

BAND 4 — heading "What it found": 6 result cards in a row. Each shows the small ID at top, a large verdict word in its color with a matching status icon, and one plain sentence:
CMP-01 — green (#16A34A) verdict "Advance" — "Passed all eight criteria."
CMP-02 — green (#16A34A) verdict "Advance, just" — "Passed, with some values exactly on the limit."
CMP-03 — amber (#D97706) verdict "Hold" — "Heart-channel signal at 0.62 µM (limit 1.0)."
CMP-04 — red (#DC2626) verdict "Reject" — "Positive DNA-damage (Ames) test: a hard stop."
CMP-05 — blue (#2563EB) verdict "Advance with caveats" — "Large and oily (MW 548.6, cLogP 5.6): advisory only."
CMP-06 — amber (#D97706) verdict "Hold" — "Drug-interaction risk: CYP3A4 at 0.45 µM."
Small note at the right of the heading: "Hard safety failures stop a compound; size rules only add a caveat."

BOTTOM BAND — three short panels:
"Trust, but verify" — "An independent checker re-ran the checks and plain code graded the result: 6 of 6 correct."
"Honest wording" — "Where evidence was incomplete, it withdrew its confidence score and deferred to qualified human reviewers."
"Getting better each run" — "The lesson saved for next time: Probe the chemistry toolkit first; if a check can't run, mark it unassessed."

FOOTER (small, centered): "The takeaway: A tool that knows when not to decide is safer than one that always answers."

TEXT DISCIPLINE: use ONLY the words given above in quotes plus the headings. Do NOT add any slogans, taglines, mottos, handwritten notes, brand lines, decorative words, extra footers or invented statistics. Every word spelled exactly as given and legible at 4K.

Visual rules: generous whitespace, strong hierarchy (title > band headings > plain sentences > tiny grey technical labels), verdict colors only on the result cards, soft blue/teal section tints, flat friendly line icons. No people, no faces, no photos.
